newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian human rights leader needs heart surgery.
newsitem.headline: Russian human rights leader needs heart surgery.

text.p: Russia's leading human rights campaigner, parliamentarian Sergei Kovalyov, plans to travel to the United States this weekend for heart surgery, Itar-Tass news said on Saturday.

"Kovalyov will undergo a most complicated and rare operation, which can only be carried out in a fully qualified way by specialists at an American cardiological clinic," Tass quoted fellow human rights activist Valery Borshchev as saying.
The 66-year-old Kovalyov, who was due to leave Moscow on Sunday, had a serious heart attack in July and spent more than a month in Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital.
He has been suffering from ischaemia, a condition under which blocked arteries cannot circulate enough blood to the heart muscles.

The same problem put President Boris Yeltsin, 65, in hospital twice last year. Yeltsin announced on Thursday that he would undergo surgery later this month at Moscow's Cardiological Centre, but it is unclear just how serious his condition is.

Kovalyov, who has a history of health problems, gained international recognition after his highly critical stance on Yeltsin's military campaign in rebel Chechnya. He was at the time the president's human rights commissioner.
He championed human rights as a dissident with Nobel Prize winner Andrei Sakharov in the 1970s and served 10 years in labour camps and exile which contributed to his ill health.
